scope: Theorem 12.3 (Torus plates and square-integrable forcing) of the manuscript “Incompressible Box Transport and Finite Computation” (preprints/Incompressible-Box-Transport-and-Finite-Computation-October-6-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2505dc09d3f2c24b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 53. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a positive computable ν. Every deterministic one-tape machine with finitely specified tape, blank outside a finite set, effectively determines a smooth mean-zero general force on T3 = R3/Z3, with bounded mixed derivatives and period one for t ≥ 1. Its zero-data Navier–Stokes solution is globally smooth and unique among smooth solutions, with pressure normalized to mean zero and constructed pressure zero. For P∗ = (1/4, 1/2, 1/4) and X(t) = Φt(P∗), the event ∃t ≥ 0 : X1(t) (mod 1) ∈ (1/2, 7/8) (41) is equivalent to halting. A separate effective force has the same zero data, event, uniqueness and mean-zero property, is supported in one compact sub-box of (0, 1)3, has all mixed derivatives bounded, and satisfies ∥ b f(t, ·)∥∞ = O((1 + t)−2/3 ). (42) In particular b f ∈ L2([0, ∞) × T3).
